overview: Thin Thanksgiving trading saw a broad commodity rebound as LME metals led the recovery from Wednesday's rout. Zinc surged 3.5% to $3,511 per tonne — the session's standout — after Nyrstar announced the closure of its Budel smelter in the Netherlands, removing approximately 160,000 tonnes of annual capacity from Europe's second-largest zinc plant. Nickel jumped 3.7% to $15,725, copper rose 1.9% to $5.38 per pound ($11,867 per tonne), and tin gained 2.0% to $37,930 — partial recoveries from Wednesday's sharp losses. Gold spot steadied at $3,567, up 0.9% from Wednesday's 15-month low, as the dollar eased slightly during the US holiday. Silver edged up 0.4% to $41.50. Platinum rose 0.8% to $1,291; palladium gained 1.4% to $874. Brent crude's January contract settled at approximately $97 per barrel — up 2.1% — after a Houthi drone attack struck Saudi Arabia's Jazan refinery complex near the Yemen border. WTI rose to $85. Bitcoin recovered above $60,000, rising 2.8% to approximately $60,400; Ethereum gained 3.6% to $1,699. US equities were closed for Thanksgiving.

OPEC+ ministers meet Sunday November 29 to decide 2027 output quotas, with no production agreement in place beyond December 2026 — the meeting is widely expected to extend current cuts into early 2027 but disagreements over baseline quotas among UAE, Iraq and Kazakhstan remain unresolved. The Houthi drone strike on Saudi Arabia's Jazan refinery — the first successful attack on Saudi refining infrastructure in over a year — adds further geopolitical risk premium to crude. Iran's Strait of Hormuz campaign continues with 266 vessels now on Tehran's blacklist. US grains markets were closed for Thanksgiving — corn at 456 cents, wheat at 584 cents and soybeans at 1,236 cents remain at Wednesday's settlements. Newcastle coal was flat at $145. ICE cocoa gained approximately 3.5% to $4,900 per tonne on short covering from 4.5-month lows, with Ivory Coast mid-crop concerns providing structural support. The Fear and Greed Index remains in extreme fear territory despite the session's rebound. The December 9–10 FOMC meeting looms as the next major catalyst.

watchItems.title: Houthi drone strike on Saudi Jazan refinery pushes Brent January contract to $97 — first successful attack on Saudi refining infrastructure in over a year
watchItems.text: Brent crude's January contract settled at approximately $97 per barrel on Thursday — up 2.1% — after a Houthi drone attack struck Saudi Arabia's Jazan refinery complex near the Yemen border. The attack was the first successful strike on Saudi refining infrastructure in over a year and was claimed by the Houthis as retaliation for Saudi participation in the US-led maritime coalition in the Red Sea. The January contract expires November 30 and carries a roughly $5 premium over February ($92), reflecting near-term supply anxiety. Goldman Sachs's December Brent forecast of $105 and $140 risk scenario remain operative. Iran's Strait of Hormuz campaign continues with 266 vessels now on Tehran's blacklist. Three US carrier strike groups remain in the Gulf. OPEC+ meets Sunday.

watchItems.title: LME metals stage broad rebound from Wednesday's rout — zinc +3.5% on Nyrstar Budel smelter closure, nickel +3.7%
watchItems.text: LME metals staged a broad recovery on Thursday, led by zinc surging 3.5% to $3,511 per tonne after Nyrstar announced the closure of its Budel smelter in the Netherlands — Europe's second-largest zinc plant with approximately 160,000 tonnes of annual capacity. The closure intensifies the structural supply deficit signalled by deeply negative treatment charges. Nickel jumped 3.7% to $15,725, copper rose 1.9% to $5.38 per pound ($11,867 per tonne), and tin gained 2.0% to $37,930. The rebound came in thin Thanksgiving trade with US markets closed, amplifying moves. Wednesday's sharp sell-off — tin down 7.2%, copper at an 11-month low — appeared overdone on a technical basis. Key question is whether the recovery holds when US markets reopen Friday.

watchItems.title: OPEC+ meets Sunday November 29 to decide 2027 output quotas with no production agreement beyond December 2026
watchItems.text: OPEC+ ministers meet Sunday November 29 to decide 2027 output policy, with no production agreement in place beyond December 2026. The meeting is widely expected to extend current cuts into early 2027, but disagreements over baseline quotas among UAE, Iraq and Kazakhstan remain unresolved. The timing is significant: Brent at $97 on new geopolitical risk (Houthi Jazan strike, Hormuz mine campaign) gives the group less incentive to add barrels, while producers pushing for higher quotas can point to supply tightness. Saudi Arabia is producing well below its preferred level. Any surprise — a failure to agree, or unexpected production increases — could move crude $5–10 in either direction.

watchItems.title: Bitcoin recovers above $60,000 as thin holiday trading lifts crypto alongside commodities
watchItems.text: Bitcoin recovered 2.8% to approximately $60,400 on Thursday, climbing back above the psychologically important $60,000 level after Wednesday's breach below that threshold. Ethereum gained 3.6% to $1,699. The recovery came in thin Thanksgiving trading as the dollar eased slightly and risk assets broadly rebounded. Bitcoin remains down approximately 25% from a month ago and 52% from its all-time high of $126,198. The Fear and Greed Index remains in extreme fear territory. Key resistance at $62,000; support at $58,000. The recovery's durability will be tested when US markets and institutional trading resume Friday.

desk.name: Gold
desk.m: Spot ~$3,567 +0.9% · bounced from Wed 15-month low of $3,474 · dollar eased on US holiday · COMEX closed Thanksgiving · Dec hike still ~98% · OPEC+ Sun
desk.sum: Gold spot steadied at approximately $3,567 per ounce on Thursday, up 0.9% from Wednesday's 15-month low, as the dollar eased slightly during the US Thanksgiving holiday. COMEX was closed but spot gold traded higher in overseas markets. The bounce was modest relative to Wednesday's 2.5% decline and followed twelve declines in thirteen sessions. December rate-hike expectations remain at approximately 98% per CME FedWatch. The dollar's pullback provided temporary relief but the structural headwinds — tight monetary policy, strong dollar, tariff risks — remain intact. Key support at $3,500; resistance at $3,600.

desk.name: Silver
desk.m: Spot ~$41.50 · modest recovery from Wed rout · gold-silver ratio narrowed slightly · COMEX closed · dollar eased on US holiday
desk.sum: Silver edged up 0.4% to approximately $41.50 per ounce on Thursday, a modest bounce from Wednesday's sharp 4.9% decline. The recovery was muted in thin Thanksgiving trade with COMEX closed. The gold-silver ratio narrowed slightly from approximately 89 to 86. Silver remains down significantly in November. The dollar's slight pullback during the US holiday helped, but industrial metal headwinds and rate-hike expectations continue to cap any sustained recovery. Key support at $40; resistance at $43.

desk.m: Jan settle ~$97 (+2.1%) · Houthi drone strike on Jazan refinery · Jan expires Nov 30 · Feb ~$92 · WTI $85 · Goldman: $105 Dec, $140 risk · OPEC+ Sun Nov 29 · Hormuz 266 blacklisted
desk.sum: Brent crude's January contract settled at approximately $97 per barrel on Thursday — up 2.1% — after a Houthi drone attack struck Saudi Arabia's Jazan refinery complex near the Yemen border. The attack was the first successful strike on Saudi refining infrastructure in over a year. WTI rose to $85. The January contract expires November 30, and the roughly $5 premium over February ($92) reflects near-term supply anxiety. Iran's Hormuz campaign continues with 266 blacklisted vessels. Goldman Sachs's December forecast of $105 and $140 risk scenario remain operative. OPEC+ ministers meet Sunday November 29 to decide 2027 output quotas.

desk.name: Copper
desk.m: LME $11,867/t · rebounded from Wed 11-month low · thin Thanksgiving trade amplified recovery · still down ~16% in Nov · OPEC+ Sun
desk.sum: Copper rose 1.9% to $5.38 per pound ($11,867 per tonne LME) on Thursday, rebounding from Wednesday's 11-month low in thin Thanksgiving trade. The recovery was partly technical — Wednesday's 2.2% decline appeared overdone — but macro headwinds remain intact. Copper is still down approximately 16% in November. The dollar's slight pullback during the US holiday helped. Physical conditions remain tight, with record Yangshan premiums. Key support at $5.26/lb ($11,596/t); resistance at $5.45/lb ($12,000/t).

desk.name: Coal
desk.m: Flat at $145 in thin Thanksgiving trade · Brent at $97 supportive for coal substitution · LNG supply crisis intact · still up ~36% YTD · OPEC+ Sun
desk.sum: Newcastle coal held flat at $145 per tonne on Thursday in thin Thanksgiving trade. Brent crude's advance to $97 on the Houthi Jazan refinery strike is supportive for coal-to-gas substitution economics. Coal remains up approximately 36% year to date. QatarEnergy's force majeure continues through at least end-December 2026. OPEC+ meets Sunday. The near-term outlook is range-bound between energy complex support and the broader macro headwinds that have weighed on industrial commodities through November.

desk.name: Platinum
desk.m: Spot ~$1,291 · modest bounce from Wed 15-month low · South African supply still constrained · thin holiday trade · dollar eased
desk.sum: Platinum rose 0.8% to approximately $1,291 per ounce on Thursday, bouncing modestly from Wednesday's 15-month low. The recovery was thin-market-driven during the US holiday. South African mine supply remains constrained, and hydrogen electrolysis demand provides structural long-term support. The dollar's slight pullback helped, but platinum remains down approximately 9% in November. Key support at $1,260; resistance at $1,310.

desk.name: Palladium
desk.m: Spot ~$874 · recovery from Wed's $843 · still below $900 · EV transition headwind persists · thin trade amplified move
desk.sum: Palladium gained 1.4% to approximately $874 per ounce on Thursday, recovering partially from Wednesday's 3.1% decline. The bounce came in thin Thanksgiving trade with the dollar easing slightly. Palladium remains below $900, reflecting the structural headwind from the EV transition — fewer catalytic converters needed in battery-electric vehicles. Down approximately 38% year on year. Key support at $843; resistance at $900.

desk.name: Hormuz Terminal
desk.m: Houthi drone strike on Jazan refinery · 266 vessels blacklisted · IRGC mine campaign ongoing · Brent $97 · Goldman: $105 Dec, $140 risk · 3 US carriers · OPEC+ Sun Nov 29
desk.sum: The Strait of Hormuz crisis intensified on Thursday as a Houthi drone attack struck Saudi Arabia's Jazan refinery complex near the Yemen border — the first successful strike on Saudi refining infrastructure in over a year. This follows Wednesday's IRGC mine attacks on two tankers and an LNG carrier. Brent rose to $97. Iran's vessel blacklist stands at 266, aiming to deny salvage services to attacked ships. IMF PortWatch recorded just 1 transit on November 22, compared to a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. Three US carrier strike groups remain in the Gulf. OPEC+ meets Sunday.
desk.src: straits.live · Insurance Journal · gCaptain · UKMTO · JMIC · Reuters

desk.name: Corn
desk.m: Unchanged — US markets closed Thanksgiving · Wed settle 456¢ · fund short-covering trend intact · Black Sea disruption supports · OPEC+ Sun
desk.sum: US grain markets were closed Thursday for Thanksgiving. December corn remains at Wednesday's settlement of 456 cents per bushel. The fund short-covering and export demand trends that lifted corn 1.3% on Wednesday remain intact. Black Sea maritime disruption continues to support US export competitiveness. Corn has been the most resilient grain through November's commodity sell-off. Markets reopen Friday for a shortened session. Key resistance at 460 cents; support at 450 cents.

desk.name: Wheat
desk.m: Unchanged — US markets closed Thanksgiving · Wed settle 584¢ · SovEcon: Russia exports 36Mt · Black Sea disruption ongoing · OPEC+ Sun
desk.sum: US grain markets were closed Thursday for Thanksgiving. December SRW wheat remains at Wednesday's settlement of 584 cents per bushel. SovEcon's Russian wheat export estimate of 36 million tonnes — below the USDA forecast — continues to provide structural support. Black Sea disruption remains a factor. Dollar eased slightly during the holiday, a modest positive for grain exports when markets reopen Friday for a shortened session. Key support at 575 cents; resistance at 590 cents.

desk.name: Soybean
desk.m: Unchanged — US markets closed Thanksgiving · Wed settle 1,236¢ · meal support intact · export commitments up ~80% YoY · OPEC+ Sun
desk.sum: US grain markets were closed Thursday for Thanksgiving. January soybeans remain at Wednesday's settlement of 1,236 cents per bushel. Soybean meal strength continues to provide structural support. US soybean export commitments remain up approximately 80% year on year. The dollar eased slightly during the holiday, a modest positive for US export competitiveness. Markets reopen Friday for a shortened session. Key support at 1,220 cents; resistance at 1,245 cents.

desk.name: Cryptocurrencies
desk.m: ETH $1,699 +3.6% · BTC recovered above $60k · down ~25% from 1 month ago · Fear & Greed extreme · thin holiday trade · OPEC+ Sun
desk.sum: Bitcoin recovered 2.8% to approximately $60,400 on Thursday, climbing back above the psychologically important $60,000 level after Wednesday's breach below that threshold. Ethereum gained 3.6% to $1,699. The recovery came in thin Thanksgiving trading as the dollar eased slightly. Bitcoin remains down approximately 25% from a month ago and 52% from its all-time high of $126,198. The Fear and Greed Index remains in extreme fear territory. The recovery's durability will be tested when institutional trading resumes Friday. Key resistance at $62,000; support at $58,000.

desk.name: LNG
desk.m: JKM eased to ~$28 from $29 · TTF ~$28.5 · HH ~$3.40 · Houthi Jazan strike adds supply risk · QatarEnergy FM continues · Brent $97 raises oil-linked contract pricing
desk.sum: The Asian LNG spot JKM eased slightly to approximately $28 per MMBtu from $29 earlier in the week. TTF sits near $28.50; Henry Hub near $3.40. The Houthi drone strike on Saudi Arabia's Jazan refinery adds further geopolitical risk to energy supply logistics. QatarEnergy's force majeure extends through at least end-December 2026. Brent crude's advance to $97 raises oil-linked LNG contract pricing. OPEC+ meets Sunday to decide 2027 output policy. The LNG supply-side picture remains tight heading into Northern Hemisphere winter.
desk.src: S&P Global Platts · Global LNG Hub · Trading Economics

desk.name: Sulfur
desk.m: FOB Kuwait ~$765 · Hormuz mine campaign ongoing · 266 vessels blacklisted · Houthi Jazan strike · Brent $97 · OPEC+ Sun
desk.sum: Sulfur remains elevated at approximately $1,200 per tonne CFR Southeast Asia. The ongoing Hormuz mine campaign and Thursday's Houthi strike on Saudi Arabia's Jazan refinery maintain supply-side risk for Middle Eastern sulfur logistics. FOB Kuwait holds near $765 (KPC). Iran's vessel blacklist at 266 ships continues to constrain salvage and transit operations in the Gulf. Brent crude's advance to $97 supports the petroleum-sulfur production dynamic. OPEC+ meets Sunday.

desk.name: Potash
desk.m: BPC India $383 CFR · China benchmark ~$348 · grains closed Thanksgiving · Brent $97 raises input costs · OPEC+ Sun
desk.sum: Muriate of potash (MOP) CFR Brazil holds at approximately $358 per tonne. BPC's India contract remains approximately $25 above China's 2026 benchmark at $383 per tonne CFR. US grain markets were closed Thursday for Thanksgiving, leaving fertiliser demand signals unchanged from Wednesday's mixed session. Belarus and Russia still account for about 40% of global supply despite Western sanctions. Brent crude's advance to $97 on the Houthi Jazan strike modestly raises potash production input costs.

desk.name: Antimony
desk.m: China suspension extended to Jan 27, 2027 · Rotterdam $18,300–19,000/t · prices stabilised · underlying controls remain · 11 days until old deadline passed
desk.sum: Chinese antimony (#1 ingot) holds near ¥92,000 per tonne. China's two-month extension of its US-specific export-control suspension to January 27, 2027 has stabilised prices — the original November 27 deadline passes today with no disruption. Overseas antimony sits at approximately $18,300–19,000 per tonne in Rotterdam. The two-month window maintains strategic leverage while avoiding an outright supply rupture. The underlying licensing regimes remain in force. China produces close to half of global mined antimony.

desk.name: Gallium & Germanium
desk.m: China suspension extended to Jan 27, 2027 · China domestic Ga ~$460/kg · 4.5x premium persists · Alcoa Wagerup FID but not producing · original Nov 27 deadline passes today
desk.sum: Gallium holds near $2,100 per kilogram outside China, with Chinese domestic gallium at approximately $460 per kilogram — a roughly 4.5x premium. The original November 27 export-control deadline passes today with no disruption following China's two-month extension to January 27, 2027. The underlying licensing regimes remain in force during the suspension. China produces approximately 99% of global gallium and 60–80% of germanium. Alcoa's Wagerup gallium refinery has taken FID but is not yet producing. The rolling extensions maintain strategic leverage while avoiding a trade rupture.

desk.name: Vanadium
desk.m: Steady at $5.30 · upstream tightness · VRFB adoption timeline uncertain · China-Russia-SA control 90%+ · gallium/germanium deadline passes today without disruption
desk.sum: Vanadium pentoxide (V₂O₅) holds at approximately $5.30 per pound in Europe, supported by persistent upstream tightness. The original gallium, germanium and antimony export-control deadline passes today without disruption following China's two-month extension to January 27, 2027. The long-term bull case rests on vanadium redox flow batteries (VRFBs) for grid-scale energy storage, but adoption timing remains uncertain. China, Russia and South Africa control over 90% of supply.

desk.name: Cocoa
desk.m: Short covering rally from 4.5-month lows · Ivory Coast mid-crop may fall 42–50% YoY · ICE stocks at 2.5-year high · $5,000 resistance · thin holiday trade
desk.sum: ICE cocoa gained approximately 3.5% to $4,900 per tonne on Thursday, rallying on short covering from 4.5-month lows in thin Thanksgiving trade. Ivory Coast's Sodexam projects 2026/27 output down 21–25% due to El Niño, and Reuters sources suggest the mid-crop could fall 42–50% year on year. Against this, ICE warehouse inventories sit at a 2.5-year high of approximately 3.8 million bags. The $5,000 level serves as psychological resistance. The rebound reflects technical positioning rather than a fundamental shift.

desk.name: Cobalt
desk.m: Flat near $32,500 · Rotterdam $16–17/lb · DRC logistics disruption ongoing · NMC-to-LFP shift structural headwind · market in surplus
desk.sum: Cobalt is estimated near $32,500 per tonne, flat. Rotterdam standard-grade cobalt metal sits at $16–17 per pound. The DRC bridge collapse continues to have secondary effects on cobalt logistics. The NMC-to-LFP battery chemistry shift weighs on the structural demand outlook. The LME base metals rebound on Thursday — led by zinc and nickel — has not lifted cobalt meaningfully given its own fundamentals. The market remains in structural surplus.

desk.name: Lithium
desk.m: Flat near ¥87,000 · structural oversupply persists · Goldman: 444k t global surplus by 2028 · destocking continues · ¥85,000 support
desk.sum: Chinese lithium carbonate holds near ¥87,000 per tonne, flat. Structural oversupply remains the dominant theme, with Goldman Sachs projecting a 444,000-tonne global surplus by 2028. SMM data shows sustained monthly destocking. The EU's plan to cap Chinese EV imports at 350,000 units per year adds a demand headwind. The LME base metals rebound has not extended to lithium given its separate demand dynamics. Supply ramp-ups in Australia and South America continue to outpace demand growth. The ¥85,000 zone represents next major support.

desk.name: Rubber
desk.m: $2.55/kg · SE Asia supply tight · fungal blight ongoing · Brent $97 raises synthetic rubber costs · auto demand solid
desk.sum: Natural rubber (RSS3) trades near $2,550 per tonne ($2.55/kg), range-bound. Southeast Asian supply remains tight, with Thailand, Indonesia and Malaysia producing 70% of global latex and still affected by Pestalotiopsis fungal leaf blight. Brent crude's advance to $97 on the Houthi Jazan strike further raises synthetic rubber production costs, tilting the balance toward natural rubber. Auto-sector demand remains solid. OPEC+ meets Sunday to decide output policy.

desk.name: Uranium
desk.m: Spot ~$91 near 9-month high · term price $98/lb near record · IAEA: 78 reactors under construction · AI demand structural · miners sliding despite price strength
desk.sum: Uranium spot edged higher to approximately $91 per pound U₃O₈, approaching a nine-month high. Long-term contract prices sit at $98 per pound — approaching the $100 milestone. Despite spot prices holding above $90 for most of November, uranium miners (URNM ETF) have continued to slide, reflecting rate sensitivity and ETF-driven selling. The IAEA counts 78 reactors under construction worldwide. AI data-centre power demand remains a structural driver. Uranium's supply-driven narrative has been largely insulated from the broader commodity sell-off.

desk.name: Rare Earths
desk.m: Pr-Nd prices on the rise per SMM · ex-China NdPr below $110/kg · gallium/germanium deadline passes today · downstream demand sluggish
desk.sum: Neodymium-praseodymium (NdPr) oxide holds at approximately $72 per kilogram domestically in China. SMM reports that Pr-Nd prices are on the rise, with suppliers holding firm and limiting price concessions. Ex-China NdPr prices remain below $110 per kilogram. The original gallium, germanium and antimony export-control deadline passes today without disruption. Downstream magnetic material orders remain sluggish. The broader LME metals rebound has not meaningfully lifted rare earth sentiment.

desk.name: Manganese
desk.m: South Africa 37% · Gabon 18% · miners holding firm · CIF China flat · LME metals rebound may lift steel demand sentiment
desk.sum: Manganese ore (44% Mn content) trades near $4.40 per dry metric tonne unit CIF China, flat. Miners continue holding a firm pricing stance. South Africa supplies about 37% of global ore and Gabon 18%. Steel production consumes 90% of manganese demand. Thursday's LME base metals rebound — zinc up 3.5%, nickel up 3.7% — may provide a modest lift to steel demand sentiment. Key question is whether the recovery in base metals sustains beyond the thin holiday session.

desk.name: Nickel
desk.m: LME 3M ~$15,725 · strongest rebound in LME complex · oversold bounce from Wed 1-year low · Indonesian RKAB uncertainty · global surplus continues
desk.sum: LME nickel jumped 3.7% to $15,725 per tonne on Thursday, leading the base metals rebound alongside zinc in thin Thanksgiving trade. The recovery came from oversold conditions after nickel touched a one-year low. Indonesian RKAB mining quota uncertainty persists — potential tightening provides a floor while the global nickel surplus from Indonesian NPI and HPAL expansions caps upside. The move was amplified by thin liquidity. Key question is whether the recovery holds when full trading resumes Friday. Key support at $15,175.

desk.name: Tin
desk.m: LME 3M ~$37,930 · partial recovery from Wed's 7.2% plunge · still near 1-year low · Myanmar ban constraining supply · thin trade amplified bounce
desk.sum: LME tin gained 2.0% to approximately $37,930 per tonne on Thursday, partially recovering from Wednesday's 7.2% plunge to a one-year low. The bounce came in thin Thanksgiving trade. The recovery is modest relative to Wednesday's sharp decline — tin remains near its lowest level in a year. Structural supply constraints from Myanmar's Wa State mining ban and Indonesian export licensing tightness persist. The thin market amplified Thursday's move just as it amplified Wednesday's sell-off. Key support at $36,710; resistance at $39,000.

desk.name: Zinc
desk.m: LME 3M ~$3,511 · Nyrstar Budel smelter closure — 160,000 t/yr capacity removed · session's standout · TCs deeply negative · structural deficit intensified
desk.sum: LME zinc surged 3.5% to approximately $3,511 per tonne on Thursday — the session's standout performer — after Nyrstar announced the closure of its Budel smelter in the Netherlands. Budel is Europe's second-largest zinc plant with approximately 160,000 tonnes of annual capacity. The closure intensifies the structural supply deficit signalled by deeply negative treatment charges that have forced continued smelter curtailments outside China. Zinc is still up approximately 10% year on year. The move highlights how supply-side disruptions can override macro headwinds. Key support at $3,389; resistance at $3,600.

desk.name: Tungsten
desk.m: Rotterdam APT $2,750 · China FOB $1,845 · Western ~3.5x China · export-control deadline passes today without disruption
desk.sum: European tungsten APT holds at $2,750 per mtu in Rotterdam, while Chinese FOB sits at $1,845 per mtu — Western prices remain roughly 3.5 times Chinese domestic levels. The original gallium, germanium and antimony export-control deadline of November 27 passes today without disruption following China's two-month extension. The market continues to reflect the fragmentation created by China's export controls. The rolling extensions maintain the status quo while keeping strategic leverage intact.

desk.name: Helium
desk.m: Up 358% YTD · Ras Laffan repair 3–5 years · Houthi Jazan strike adds energy supply risk · Hormuz mine campaign ongoing · 266 vessels blacklisted
desk.sum: Grade-A helium trades near $390 per thousand cubic feet, at critical levels. Thursday's Houthi drone strike on Saudi Arabia's Jazan refinery — the first successful attack on Saudi refining infrastructure in over a year — adds further geopolitical risk to energy supply routes that also carry helium. Iran's Hormuz mine campaign continues with 266 vessels blacklisted. QatarEnergy's Ras Laffan facility repairs remain estimated at 3–5 years. Helium is up approximately 358% year to date, driven almost entirely by Qatar supply disruptions.

desk.name: Phosphate
desk.m: OCP 30% global · DAP $560/t · sulfur cost surge pressuring economics · grains closed Thanksgiving
desk.sum: Phosphate rock trades near $120 per tonne FOB Morocco, with Morocco's OCP Group controlling about 30% of global trade. DAP prices sit near $560 per tonne CFR India. The sulfur price surge continues to pressure phosphate production economics. US grain markets were closed Thursday for Thanksgiving, leaving fertiliser demand signals unchanged. Brent crude's advance to $97 further reduces the probability of Middle Eastern sulfur supply normalising. OPEC+ meets Sunday.

Bitcoin recovered 2.8% to approximately $60,400 on Thursday, climbing back above the psychologically important $60,000 level in thin Thanksgiving trading as the dollar eased slightly.
LME nickel fell 2.5% on Thursday to $14,800 per tonne, extending its decline to a two-year low as Indonesian NPI exports surged and the global surplus widened to an estimated 180,000 tonnes in 2026.

LME nickel actually jumped 3.7% to $15,725 per tonne on Thursday, leading the base metals rebound alongside zinc in thin Thanksgiving trade. The recovery came from oversold conditions after nickel touched a one-year low.

OPEC+ ministers meet Sunday November 29 to decide 2027 output quotas, with no production agreement in place beyond December 2026 — the meeting is widely expected to extend current cuts into early 2027.

Newcastle thermal coal surged 4% to $151 per tonne on Thursday as the Houthi attack on Saudi Arabia's Jazan refinery lifted the entire energy complex, with coal following Brent crude's advance to $97.

Newcastle coal actually held flat at $145 per tonne on Thursday in thin Thanksgiving trade. While Brent rose to $97 on the Houthi Jazan strike, coal was range-bound as the broader macro headwinds continued to weigh.
